Recommendations of Fifth Pay Commission for Pensioners 
*308. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTACHARJEE : Will the Minister of 
FINANCE be pleased to state : 
(a) the number of recommendations made by the Fifth Pay Commission 
with regard to the Central Government pensioners together with the details 
thereof: 
(b) the number of recommendations together with the details thereof 
rejected by the Central Government: and 
(c) what are the reasons for rejection ? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL): (a) to (c) Major recommendations of the Fifth 
Central Pay Commission regarding pensionary benefits of retired civilian Central 
Government employees numbering 11 are summarised below:— 
1. Payment of Pension (a\ 67% of the last pay drawn. This was to be 
met to the extent of 50% through the normal scheme of Pension to 
be funded by Government with the balance 17% being made by 
contributions from the employees to a Pension Fund. 
2. Additional Pension @ 0.5% of emoluments for each completed six 
monthly period of sen ice or 1% for each additional year of sen ice 
beyond 33 years. 
3. Removal of ceilings on Pension/Family Pension and Gratuities. 
4. Payment of Gratuity on the basis of Pay and DA on the date of 
retirement. 
5. Payment of Family Pension at a uniform rate of 30% of pay. Minimum 
Family Pension to be Rs. 1220. 
6. 100% neutralisation of cost of living through Dearness Relief and 
extension of this to employed family pensioners also. 
7. Raising of the limit of commutation of Pension for civilian employees 
from 33.1/3% to 40%. Commuted portion to be restored after 12 
yean, instead of 15 years as at present. 
8. Grant of absolute parity between pre and post 1-1-1986 pensioners 
and modified parity for pre and post 1-1-1996 pensioners. 
9. Grant of minimum pension of 50% of the minimum pay of the post 
held at the time of retirement as revised from time to time. 
25 

RAJYA SABHA [ 11 December. 2001 ] 
10. Payment of a fixed medical allowance of Rs. 100 per month for 
pensioners residing in areas not covered by CGHS. 
11. Computation of pensionary benefits with reference to the average 
emoluments during the last 6 months of service. 
Five recommendations of the Fifth Central Pay Commission have, so far, 
been rejected by the Government taking into account the existing pension formula, 
legal and financial implications, etc. Relevant details in respect of the 
recommendations are as under:— 
1. Restoration of commuted portion of pension after 12 years instead of the 
existing period of 15 years. 
The pay commission had recommended that the period of restoration of 
commutation of pension needs to be reduced from 15 years to 12 years. This 
recommendation was examined and not accepted taking into account all relevant 
factors and the financial implications thereof. 
2. Grant of additional pension at the rate of 0.5% of emoluments for each 
completed six monthly period of service or 1% for each additional year of 
sen ice in excess of 33 years. 
This recommendation could not be accepted as any departure from the 
present pension formula would have a ttracted the Suprem e Court Judgement 
delivered in D'.S. Nakra's case and its implementation had significant financial 
implications of a recurring nature. Besides, implementation of this recommendation 
would have been difficult on account of non-availability of records and would 
also have created two classes of pensioners within the same homogenous group. 
3. Calculation of pension on average emoluments for six months. 
This recommendation was rejected as acceptance there of would have 
meant changing the existing pension formula without any concomitant benefits. 
4. Interest on delayed payment of pension. 
This recommendation could not be accepted as no interest is payable 
even in the case of delayed payment of pay and allowances. 
5. Standing Committee of Voluntary Or ganisations to have the same 
machinery for implementation of decisions as in the case of JCM including 
that of Reference of Board of Arbitration. 
Taking various factors into account the Government has not been able to 
accept this recommendation.

Impact of China's Entry into WTO on Indian Industries 
2290. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that China has been allowed entry into WTO; 
(b) if so. whether Government have analysed its impact on Indian 
industries particularly electronics, small scale, food and agriculture; and 
(c) the steps being taken to absorb the Chinese impact? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDI): (a) Yes. Sir. The Fourth Ministerial meeting 
of WTO held at Doha. Qatar, decided on 10th October, 2001 to accept the accession 
instruments indicating the terms and conditions of Peoples Republic of China's 
Membership in WTO. Subsequently, on 11th November. 2001 the Government of PR 
China accepted the protocol done at Doha. Accordingly. PR China's accession to 
WTO will enter into force on Ilth December. 2001, one month after the acceptance of 
protocol by the Government of PR China. 
(b) and (c) India has been actively involved in the G ATT/WHO accession process 
of China which started in 1986. A bilateral agreement was signed with China on 22nd 
February. 2000 where tariff and other concessions were agreed to by China with India. 
There may not be any immediate impact on Indian industries on account of China's 
accession to WTO as such, because India and China have already been exchanging 
Most Favoured Nation (MFN) Treatment and because the concessions had to be given 
unilaterally by China on entry to WTO and no reciprocal commitments were involved on 
the part of India or any other WTO Member. The effects of China's accession to WTO 
should, therefore, be beneficial to Indian exports since conditions of market access 
including in respect of tariffs in the Chinese market will significantly improve. The main policy 
emphasis is to make the Indian industry globally competitive in addition to regular 
monitoring of imports, particularly consumer goods.

BALASAHEB VTKHE PATIL): (a)There are reports about shortage of coins in 
some parts of the country. However, there is no shortage of Bank notes in the

during the current year to meet the shortage of Rs. 5 coins.

imported to meet the gap between demand and supply of coins in 
the country.

2382.DRAK.PATEL: 
SHRIRAJUPARMAR: 
DR. ARUN KUMAR SARMA : 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the present policy of Government regarding fixation of royalty rates of 
crude oil and gas: 
(b) whether Government have any plan to revise the same; 
(c) if so, whether any committees have been set up for the purpose and if 
so, the findings of those Committees; and 
(d) what is Government's opinion regarding the suggestions of these 
Committees? 
141 

RAJYA SABHA [ 11 December. 2001 ] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS (SHRI SANTOSH GANGWAR): (a) to (d) Royalty on crude oil 
and natural gas is payable at the rates fixed by the Central Government from time 
to time pursuant to the provisions of Oil Fields (Regulation and Development) 
Act. 1948 and the Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules. 1959 framed thereunder, as 
amended from time to time. Under provisions of the above said Rules, royalty on 
the crude oil and natural gas produced from offshore is payable to Central 
Government and that from onshore area s to the State Government. The Rules 
also provide that the Royalty on crude oil and natural gas cannot exceed 20 per 
cent of the selling price at well-head. Royalty on crude oil is payable on flat rate 
basis and on ad-valorem basis for natural gas for the cases where Petroleum 
Exploration Licenses (PELs) and Petroleum Mining Leases (PMLs). other than 
the PELs/PMLs under the New Exploration Licensing Polio.' (NELP) or on NELP 
terms, had been granted to Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd. (ONGC) and Oil 
India Limited (OIL). Royalty on crude oil is payable on fiat rate basis and on 
ad-valorem basis for natural gas for the cases, where PELs and PMLs. other 
than the PELs/PMLs under NELP. are held by Private Companies pursuant to the 
Production Sharing Contracts signed by Government of India. Royally on both 
crude oil and natural gas is payable on  ad-valorem basis for the cases, where 
PELs have been granted under NELP or NELP terms. A Committee to evolve a 
new scheme of royalty on crude oil applicable with effect from 1-4-1998 was 
constituted by the Government. The committee has submitted its report on 26-
11 -2001, which is under examination by the Government.
